notes: Background: mid-market CCaaS vendor focused on omnichannel agent assist. Primary app is an agent UI that issues actions (create ticket, add note, issue refund, escalate to fraud queue) via backend APIs.
Current ask: reliable tool-calling layer from LLM assistant -> support backend (HelixTicket API + Stripe/Adyen) with strong idempotency, audit trails, and sub-300ms median UI response for sync flows.
Constraints: PCI scope for refunds — legal insists on on-prem staging for payment-related POC; EU data residency for EU customers; SSO (SAML) and 3yr audit log retention requested.
Scale profile: typical steady-state 120 rps of agent actions, peaks up to 1.2k rps during promos (Black Friday style). Need graceful degradation under spikes (queue + async fallback).
Latency/throughput targets: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms for tool-calling path when running in dedicated cluster. Throughput target for POC: 500 actions/sec sustained for 30m.
Cost sensitivity: CFO asking for cost per ticket telemetry; target unit economics to allow < $0.05 incremental cost per handled ticket (including inference + infra).

Model preferences: prefer recent open-source Llama-family or commercial equivalent; ability to route cheap reranker/embedding calls to hosted low-cost models and keep tool-calls on dedicated private runtime.

Reliability needs: automatic fallback to a queued async worker when runtime overloaded; circuit-breaker + canary on model changes; deterministic function-calling payloads for backend idempotency checks.
Security notes: require KMS-backed key rotation for API keys, field-level redaction for PCI data, and signed audit events stored in customer-managed S3 with retention policy.
Quote from CTO (call 2026-01-22): "Tool-calls must be auditable and reversible. If a refund is issued by the assistant, we need full trace + human approval flow for > $200 refunds."
Pilot idea: 2-week POC to validate end-to-end tool-calling: agent UI -> Redwood runtime -> HelixTicket + Stripe sandbox. Include replayable load test and fault injection (delay, 5xx).
Ask from SE: provide template for function-calling schemas and sample idempotency patterns; provide cost projection for both dedicated and private deployments.
Preferred integrations: HelixTicket (internal), Zendesk (some customers), Stripe/Adyen. Want Redwood to support prebuilt connectors or reference adapters.
Risk items: unknown behavior for nested tool-calls (ticket create then refund) and long-running compensating transactions; need guidance on transaction patterns and eventual consistency.
Docs/links referenced: drive deck (pricing + architecture), security FAQ, and a postmortem of a prior outage that caused ticket duplication under load (linked in Drive).
